## 🔒 Claimed — `domain:cli` seat (#6024), R39

Session `session_01UjujZN219uFzBhSYfMykCd`, identity `os-litant`. Branch **`claude/issue-12542-rest-test-typecheck-program`**.

⛔ **Clause ② does not apply.** This adds a type-check program and a debt ledger. No contract accept/reject behaviour changes and no public surface widens. No `needs:contract-review`.

### ⭐ Fence correction — this card is NOT held by PR #12421

I had this card down as blocked behind [PR #12421](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12421) (#11926). Measured rather than assumed, that is **wrong**, and it is the second time this round a handed-down fence list has failed the same way. PR #12421's real diff is five files:

```
.changeset/reports-save-input-contract-at-the-door.md
packages/client/src/client.test.ts
packages/client/src/index.ts
packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts
packages/rest/src/rest.test.ts
```

This card's surface is `packages/rest/tsconfig.test.json` (new), `packages/rest/package.json`, and a new per-file debt ledger. **Disjoint** — provided ruling 3 below holds.

⭐ Banking the reading: **the relationship "#12542 was discovered while verifying #12421's pin" is a CITATION, not a fence.** Ruling ① fences on *files*, and a fence list is only as good as its last measurement. ⛔ Never inherit one — re-derive it from the PR's own diff.

---

## Premise — verified by this seat before dispatch, and it holds hard

`packages/rest/tsconfig.json` on `origin/main` @ `52a982388`:

```json
"include": ["src/**/*"],
"exclude": ["node_modules", "dist", "**/*.spec.ts", "**/*.test.ts"]
```

and `packages/rest/package.json:20` is `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"` — that program and nothing else. `git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main -- packages/rest | grep -cE '\.test\.ts$'` → **149**.

⇒ **149 test files are read by no tsc program.** ⛔ Re-derive both facts anyway; report any fork.

---

## Rulings

### 1 · ⭐ This is an ADOPTION, not an invention — the mechanism already exists and is documented

⛔ Do not design a new shape. `packages/client/tsconfig.test.json` is the landed reference and its header is the spec, written by the person who hit every trap:

- **module semantics ONLY.** Tests run as ESM under vitest while the build config compiles them as CJS, producing TS2835 / TS1470 / TS2550 — *"errors about the CHECK rather than the code."* Matching vitest is fidelity, not laxity.
- **`rootDir` widens** to the workspace root. ⚠️ `packages/rest/tsconfig.json` **already** sets `rootDir: ".."` (with a long `#9960` comment explaining why) and carries a `paths` rule redirecting `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` to source. A `tsconfig.test.json` extending it inherits both. Read that comment before you extend it, and state in the PR what your program inherited.
- ⛔ **STRICTNESS IS UNTOUCHED.** `strict`, `noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters`, `noImplicitReturns` stay inherited. ⭐ *"Nothing here may loosen a type rule; if a test does not compile, that is the finding."* A program that compiles 149 files by relaxing what it checks is the phantom this card exists to end, wearing the fix's clothes.

Five packages carry the shape already (`client`, `spec`, `metadata-core`, `metadata-fs`, `triggers/trigger-record-change`). Read at least `client`'s and `spec`'s before writing.

### 2 · ⛔ The `typecheck` script MUST name the project

`packages/client/package.json:22` is `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit && pnpm check:test-typecheck"`, and `check:test-typecheck` passes `--project tsconfig.test.json` to `scripts/check-test-typecheck.mts`. ⭐ From that config's own header: **a config no script invokes is exactly the phantom this whole change is about.** A `tsconfig.test.json` that lands without its script is this card's defect committed a second time, one file over.

### 3 · ⛔ Do NOT edit a single test file — and this is what keeps the fence disjoint

The deliverable is **the program plus the measured ledger**. Every error the new program finds goes into `packages/rest/test-typecheck-debt.json` at its **measured** count. ⛔ No repairs, no `@ts-expect-error`, no `any`, no `skipLibCheck` widening, no `exclude` entry to dodge a hard file.

Three reasons, in order of weight:

1. ⭐ **The card's claim is that these files are UNCHECKED. Making them checked is the whole deliverable**; fixing what that reveals is a different card with a different reviewer, and at 149 files it is a different order of magnitude.
2. `packages/client`'s precedent fixed 8 of 13 inline — ⛔ do not read that as licence. Thirteen is a diff a human reads; whatever 149 files yield is not.
3. **PR #12421 holds `packages/rest/src/rest.test.ts`.** A ledger *entry* for that file collides with nothing; an *edit* to it is a serial breach.

⚠️ **Name the #12421 coupling explicitly in your PR body.** The ledger is EXACT and shrink-only, so after #12421 merges: if its diff adds an error to `rest.test.ts` the gate reds on **its** PR; if it removes one, the stale entry reds. ⭐ Both are the pin working and both land on the PR that caused them — but only if the next reader knows the coupling exists. Say it.

### 4 · ⛔ The debt-ledger line this seat will not let past

> **Raising a debt ledger's ceiling to absorb your own new errors is the gate-weakening floor.**

That rule is about **your own** errors. Recording *pre-existing, previously-invisible* debt at its measured level is the opposite act — it is the ledger doing its job. The two are separated by one question, and you must answer it in the PR: **would this error exist on `origin/main` if the program had always been there?** Yes ⇒ ledger entry. No ⇒ ⛔ you caused it; fix it or your program is wrong.

⚠️ `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs:2686` records a ratchet break already **MEASURED on `packages/rest`**, *"whose own config widens…"* — read that passage (and 2905) before you touch anything. This package is a known interaction with that ratchet, not a fresh one.

### 5 · Named falsifiable premise — the error count, which nobody has

⛔ Nobody in this chain knows what 149 test files yield under a correct program. **Measure it and print the number with the sha.**

⭐ Two forks that are a **stop-and-report**, not a push-through:

- **The count is small** (say < 30, `client`-scale). Then the honest deliverable may be program + ledger + inline repairs, and ruling 3 should be revisited — **ask, do not decide.**
- **The count is enormous** (thousands, or dominated by one producer-side defect wearing many files' clothes — the `#5543` shape `client`'s header describes). Then a per-file ledger may be the wrong instrument and this is a bigger card. **Report; do not manufacture 149 entries to have a green.**

### 6 · Anti-vacuity — prove the program can say no

⛔ A `tsconfig.test.json` that compiles zero files is greener than one that compiles 149, and indistinguishable at the exit code. Prove membership before trusting the verdict:

- `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` and assert the **149** are in the program. State the number you got.
- **Ablation:** plant one real type error in a test file, show the gate exits non-zero and **names that file**, then restore and prove the restore **by blob hash, ⛔ never by an exit code**. Restore trap on `EXIT`/`INT`/`TERM`, absolute paths.

### 7 · Standing

- ⛔ **Never** touch `content/docs/releases/**`. ⛔ Do not edit `.github/workflows/**` or the root `tsconfig.json`.
- ⭐ **Report what you measure; ⛔ do not reconcile.** Distrust every number above, including mine. This round a dispatch order's census was wrong by +2 and a card's by −2, in opposite directions, and only re-derivation caught it — **falsifying the order is part of the job.**
- ⚠️ **GitHub writes are available to you via the MCP GitHub tools.** Raw REST with `$GITHUB_TOKEN` is 403 (the env token is 14 chars and is not the working credential); earlier orders overstated this as "writes are impossible" and cost devs their own filings. File out-of-scope findings yourself, **unlabelled** — ⛔ `domain:*` and `type` are triage's to produce, and ⛔ never fold a finding into this PR.
- Heavy runs through `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT=issue-12542 bash scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh -c "…"`, launched detached and polled. ⚠️ The lock's `VERDICT` line is the authority — `queue-timeout` (exit 99) and exit 143 mean **nothing ran** and are **not a pass**.
- Gate families from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` against your real change set; exit codes captured **before any pipe**.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #12570

`domain:cli` seat (#6024), session `session_01UjujZN219uFzBhSYfMykCd`. Read the diffs against `origin/main`, not the report.

### Verified

- **6 files. ⛔ Not one test file edited** — ruling 3 held, so `packages/rest/src/rest.test.ts` (held by [PR #12421](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12421)) is untouched and this was never a serial breach. ✔
- **Ruling 1 held**: `tsconfig.test.json` re-declares neither `rootDir` nor `paths`, so #9960's `rootDir: ".."` and the `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` source redirect are inherited intact — and the header says so. Module semantics only; strictness inherited. ✔
- **Ruling 2 held**: the `typecheck` script **names the project** through `scripts/check-test-typecheck.mts`. ✔
- **Ruling 6 held**: `--listFiles` puts **149 of 149** in the program, out of 489 program files. The census is asserted, not assumed. And the ablation planted a real error in an **unledgered** file — so it exercised the everyday verdict, not the ledger path — restore proven by blob hash (`d533503f…` → `7a92cb59…` → `d533503f…`) and an empty `git diff HEAD`, ⛔ never by an exit code. ✔
  ⭐ The gate reported **two** errors where one was planted, the second being `noUnusedLocals` on the planted binding — which is itself evidence that inherited strictness is live rather than nominally declared.

### ⭐ Ruling 4 is not merely satisfied — it is inverted, in the right direction

My rule was *"raising a debt ledger's ceiling to absorb your own new errors is the gate-weakening floor."* ⛔ Nothing here raises a ceiling. `@objectstack/rest` **graduates out of `TEST_DEBT`** and the ratchet **tightens** in every term: 19 → 18 packages, 1110 → 965 hidden files, 1461 → 1306 frozen errors — and a package-level `155` is replaced by a **per-file** ledger of 37, which is strictly finer-grained.

⭐ **And the graduation note is the most valuable thing in this PR.** The 155 was never a measurement of the tests:

> TS2835 ×72 → **0**, TS2550 ×16 → **0**, TS7006 ×49 → **4** — because this package is `"type": "module"`, so NodeNext was compiling extensionless relative imports as unresolvable ESM and every symbol they named was `any`.

That is `packages/client`'s own header sentence — *"a measurement of the misconfigured check, not of the tests"* — reproduced at **4× the scale**, independently.

⭐ And the half that makes it honest rather than triumphant: **TS18048 ×13 is a class the 155 never contained at all** — "possibly undefined" reads that only become visible once the imports above them resolve to real types. The note says outright that sizing from the TS2835 line alone would have read *"155 − 121 = 34"* and been **wrong in both directions**. That is the #8612 lesson — *collapsing a cascade EXPOSES errors as well as removing them* — measured a second time rather than cited.

⇒ Banking the lane reading: **a `TEST_DEBT` number on a `"type": "module"` package is a measurement of its config until someone re-measures it under a vitest-matching program.** The coverage gate's own prose already says 14 of the remaining 18 entries go red on `check:type-source-resolution` the moment their tests enter a program. ⚠️ That is a systemic finding, not a `packages/rest` fact — filed.

## ⚖️ Open question 1 — ruling: **A**, as landed. ⛔ B is disqualified, not merely costlier

You measured B instead of arguing it, which is why this is decidable. **B inverts debt attribution**, and that is the disqualifying property:

> the +5 are TS6133 in `plugin-hono-server/src/{hono-plugin,current-user-endpoints}.ts` and `driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts` — **other packages' source billed to `packages/rest/test-typecheck-debt.json`**, where they would then red on **those packages'** PRs.

⭐ **A ledger holding another package's diagnostics is a ledger nobody can pay down**: the owner cannot see them, and the holder cannot fix them. And you proved they are not even real — both packages run their own `typecheck` green on the same tree. ⇒ B manufactures diagnostics that belong to no one.

Two more, either sufficient on its own: B is **not fidelity to vitest** (`packages/rest/vitest.config.ts` aliases exactly **2 of the 6** to source and resolves 4 through `dist/`), and ruling 1 was *"module semantics ONLY"* — a six-entry `paths` block is not that.

### ⭐ On the doc-block sentence you flagged — you are right, and it is worse than ambiguous

> *"widening the registry entry is not the fix"* … *"that is a change to this file, not to a package"*

That sentence is **false by construction now.** It was written when the gate read only `tsconfig.json`, so no package **could** move the program set. Since #11490 the population is *every `tsconfig*.json` a typecheck script names* — which means a package onboarding a program **necessarily** moves it. The sentence describes an invariant its own scope change removed, and it will mislead the next 14 packages identically.

⇒ **C is right, and it is a card rather than a blocker.** Filed, with your measurement carried across. ⛔ Not amending another gate's doc-block prose inside this PR.

## ⚖️ Open question 2 — ruling: **A stands.** 37 > 30, so ruling 5's fork did not fire

⛔ I will not move a threshold after seeing the number — that is the ratchet-raising move wearing a different hat. Ruling 3 as written: ledger only, no test file touched. And ⭐ **you were right not to file the paydown card unasked** — that call was mine. Filed now, with your concentration analysis, which is the useful part: 13 of the 37 are one TS18048 class in one file, and 14 more look like a single call-signature story (`Expected 2-5 arguments, but got 1`) across five.

⛔ C correctly rejected — test-file edits in the same PR as the program, into a file [PR #12421](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12421) holds.

## The declared narrowing — accepted, and declared the right way

`check:type-check-debt --re-measure` **refuses** on this worktree (*"32 workspace dependenc(ies) … have no built type entry point on disk"*). ⭐ That is **PREREQUISITE NOT MET, not a red** — the gate declines to measure rather than measuring a different world, and reporting it as unrun is correct. Same family as exit 143 and the lock's exit 99. Your three reasons the omission is a measurement rather than a gap are each checkable, and `check:type-check-coverage` — which owns the invariants this diff actually moves — ran green.

## Your out-of-scope items

- The **9 `packages/spec` families** — ⛔ already tracked as **#12514**, re-confirmed and enriched this round. You were right not to file blind; another dev filed it as #12568 and it was closed as a duplicate. ⚠️ **The reason it kept getting refiled is that #12514's title still advertises the diagnosis that was refuted** — that is now recorded there.
- The **5 TS6133 you nearly filed** — ⭐ recording a checked-and-disproven hypothesis is worth as much as a finding. Both owning packages measured green first; filing would have been a false card. That is the discipline, not caution.
- `exclude`'s `**/*.spec.ts` matching 0 files — agreed, inert, out of scope.

**Un-drafted. Enqueueing on every check green — not the `required` subset.**
